Optimal bidding and scheduling of AA-CAES based energy hub
considering cascaded consumption of heat
Danman Wu a, Jiayu Bai a, Wei Wei a, *, Laijun Chen b, Shengwei Mei a
a Department of Electrical Engineering, State Key Laboratory of Power Systems, Tsinghua University, Beijing, 100084, China
b Qinghai Key Lab of Ef ﬁcient Utilization of Clean Energy, Qinghai University, Xining, 810036, China

Keywords:
Advanced-adiabatic compressed air energy
storage (AA-CAES)
Energy hub
Multi-temperature heat demands
Optimal bidding
Surrogate optimization method
abstract
The increasing level of uncertainty caused by high penetration of renewable energy and the widening
gap of peak-valley demands call for the deployment of energy storage in power systems. Advanced-
adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) is a large-scale physical energy storage technology
with the merits of long lifetime, low environmental impact, and no emission. Moreover, AA-CAES works
with electricity and heat, making it an excellent choice to realize the framework of energy hub. This
paper proposes a cogeneration and storage architecture of an AA-CAES based energy hub in an industrial
park. Particularly, the cascaded use of thermal energy to supply heat demands with different tempera-
tures is modeled. A bi-level optimization model is established to study the optimal bidding and
scheduling of AA-CAES based energy hub in the day-ahead market. The upper level is the power pur-
chase and self-scheduling of the energy hub, aiming at minimizing the daily operation cost; the lower
level represents the market clearing problem which determines the electricity price based on
alternating-current optimal power ﬂow. A radial basis function based surrogate optimization method is
developed to solve the bi-level model with a nonlinear lower level problem. The problem is decomposed
into second-order cone programs and a nonlinear surrogate model which can be solved without much
computational effort. Numerical examples verify the effectiveness of the proposed method.

1. Introduction
Electricity and heat are two main forms of energy consumption.
Cogeneration can make use of waste heat during electricity gen-
eration and thus improve overall energy ef ﬁciency, so the inte-
grated power and heat system has received wide attention [ 1]. On
the other hand, the development of renewable energy and the
increased gap between peak and valley demands require ﬂexible
resources for uncertainty mitigation and peak regulation. Energy
storage is a main sort of ﬂexibility resource, but the cost of electrical
energy storage is still relatively high [ 2]. In the heat-power inte-
grated energy system, the excessive electricity can be converted
into heat that is convenient for storage, which further improves
operating ﬂexibility. As the core of the heat-power integrated en-
ergy system, energy hub (EH) plays the role of co-generation and
storage. In the existing work, an energy hub is mainly composed of
independent components such as combined-heat-and-power unit,
battery energy storage, and thermal storage tanks, etc. [ 3,4].
Advanced-adiabatic compressed air energy storage (AA-CAES) is a
large-scale clean physical energy storage technology that naturally
possesses co-generation and storage abilities, making it an ideal
realization of energy hub [ 5,6].
Traditional work on modeling AA-CAES mainly focuses on the
simulation and analysis of thermodynamics [ 7,8]. A thermody-
namic simulation model of AA-CAES system based on static and
dynamic processes of air storage is built in Ref. [ 9], where the dy-
namic compressed air storage model demonstrates the in ﬂuence of
time-varying temperature and pressure of air on performance in-
dicators like round-trip ef ﬁciency. AA-CAES con ﬁguration optimi-
zation and ef ﬁciency improvement are studied in Refs. [ 10,11].
Ref. [ 10] presents a thermodynamic model with low temperature
thermal energy storage (TES) integration, and ref. [ 11] proposes a
novel system with variable pressure ratio based on organic Rankine
cycle. Refs. [ 12,13] conduct detailed thermodynamic analysis of
multi-stage AA-CAES system. In Ref. [ 12], the in ﬂuence of design
parameters on AA-CAES system ef ﬁciency is analyzed and the
comprehensive design standard of AA-CAES is studied. Energy and

exergy analysis of AA-CAES system is discussed in Refs. [ 14,15];
results indicate that a possible way to improve ef ﬁciency and
reduce exergy destruction is to divide compression and expansion
process into more steps and using more heat exchangers between
steps. An experimental study of a pilot AA-CAES is conducted
where TES uses water as thermal energy storage working medium
in Ref. [16]. In addition to steady state thermodynamic descriptions,
dynamic modeling of AA-CAES is studied as well. For example, ref.
[17] proposes a dynamic system model with economic analysis for
MW-scale AA-CAES and applies the model in micro grid where AA-
CAES serves as emergency backup power source. Ref. [ 18] estab-
lishes a comprehensive dynamic model of supercritical CAES sys-
tem to explore transient characteristics and control methodology,
where important factors including volume effect and thermal
inertia are considered. Ref. [19] develops a simulation software tool
considering complex dynamic characteristics caused by multi-
physical processes in AA-CAES. A certain number of validated
simulation models about pneumatics, thermodynamics, heat
transfer, electrical machines and power grids are included in the
developed tool. Ref. [ 20] applies a differential-algebraic equation
constrained optimization to model a state-space set-point control
of AA-CAES under power tracking mode. The above works have
provided detailed modeling and description of all aspects inside
AA-CAES. Nonetheless, these sophisticated models are too
complicated to be used in the operational study of the integrated
energy system, because they are usually described by nonlinear
differential-algebraic equations which is computationally
challenging.
Some recent work considers AA-CAES in power system dispatch.
Ref. [ 21] formulates a bi-objective dynamic optimal power ﬂow
problem taking AA-CAES into account; the reactive power support
capability AA-CAES is explored. In Ref. [ 22], a tri-state model of AA-
CAES considering its part load characteristics is proposed and an
efﬁcient linearization method is applied. Ref. [ 23] raises a bi-level
optimal dispatch strategy for realizing the balance between sup-
ply and demand in regional micro energy system with AA-CAES,
where the upper level problem calculates the optimal initial stor-
age volume, and the lower level optimizes the hourly operation
strategy considering the thermo-economic characteristics. Sched-
uling of regional integrated energy system considering heat and
reserve provided by AA-CAES is discussed in Ref. [ 24]. In the
scheduling framework, the multi-type applications of AA-CAES and
trading strategy of energy hub operator in both external market
and internal micro-market are considered. A joint energy and
reserve optimization scheduling model is investigated for the po-
wer system with AA-CAES in Ref. [ 25]; the scheduling model takes
the limits on the reserve capacities of thermal power units and
interruptible loads caused by AA-CAES into account. An optimal
dispatch model of zero-carbon-emission micro Energy Internet
integrated with AA-CAES system is presented in Ref. [ 26], for the
purposes of reducing curtailed wind power and operation cost
compared with traditional networks. An optimization model is
developed in Ref. [ 27] to determine the performance of a hybrid
power system which includes hydro, thermal, wind and solar
powered units along with CAES facilities. Ref. [ 28] proposes a game
theory-based multi-agent capacity optimization method for an
integrated energy system (IES) with CAES to analyze the bene ﬁt
interactions. The results show that the access of CAES could
improve economic performance of the IES and the completely
cooperative game model yields better economic performance for
the whole and for individuals. Research related to optimal bidding
of CAES in electricity market is conducted in Refs. [ 29e
31]. Ref. [29]
proposes a hybrid robust-stochastic based mixed-integer linear
programming approach for optimal bidding and offering strategies
of CAES (compressed air energy storage), where the uncertainty of
market price is considered with sets of scenarios via stochastic
method and uncertainty of maximum capacity of cavern is through
robust method. A robust optimization approach is employed in
Ref. [30] to achieve the offering and bidding curves of CAES which
should be submitted to the pool market. And a two-stage stochastic
programming based method is proposed in Ref. [ 31] to solve the
optimal bidding of a generating company owning CAES, wind and
thermal units in energy and reserve markets. In the aforemen-
tioned research, the external energy carrier is electricity, and
thermal energy conversion only happens inside the AA-CAES.
The cogeneration and storage potential of AA-CAES has also
been noticed. An MILP-based combined heat and power dispatch
model of AA-CAES is established in Ref. [ 32]. AA-CAES can share its
thermal storage tank with electricity and heating system to in-
crease the ﬂexibility of the integrated energy system. Ref. [ 33]
proposes a new structure for an advanced trigenerative CAES sys-
tem, where a burner is added before the turbine to heat inlet air.
Three operation strategies of turbine are analyzed to control output
power of system under off-design conditions. Such a structure is
also studied in Refs. [ 34e36]. Ref. [ 34] derives the guideline for
designing the trigenerative CAES based on an accurate thermody-
namic model and parametric optimization; ref. [ 35] envisages the
possibility of using small-size trigenerative CAES at the demand

side; ref. [ 36] presents a trigeneration system combining AA-CAES
and heat pump to ful ﬁll cooling, heating and power supply. A
cogeneration system combining CAES, organic rankine cycle (ORC)
and hybrid compression-absorption refrigeration cycle is proposed
in Ref. [37]. The system provides cooling from exhaust hot gas using
the ORC driven refrigeration system. Ref. [ 38] investigates the
performance of AA-CAES-based combined cooling, heating, and
power generation under different operating strategies in four sce-
narios. A parametric analysis is conducted to evaluate the in ﬂuence
of key parameters on system performance. Compared with the
conventional AA-CAES, a modi ﬁed system is proposed to take
advantage of the heat of discharged air from the low-pressure
turbine in Ref. [ 39]. Ref. [ 40] reviews a variety of systems that are
either integrating CAES technology to a cogeneration system or the
CAES system itself operating as a cogeneration system, getting the
conclusion that all cogeneration systems with CAES presented good
performance. Ref. [ 41] provides a method of economic assessment
for a cogeneration system composed of CAES, organic Rankine cycle
and absorption-compression refrigeration cycle; and ref. [ 42]p r o -
poses an AA-CAES based cogeneration system to meet the
comprehensive energy demands of a latex factory, where four novel
energy supply strategies are analyzed and compared. In the above
works, the temperature of thermal demand is neglected. In the
presence of multiple thermal demands with different tempera-
tures, new model is needed to exploit the opportunity of cascaded
use of thermal energy.
This paper considers modeling and dispatching an AA-CAES
based energy hub in an industrial park. The energy hub pur-
chases electricity from the distribution system and serves electric
load and thermal demands with two different temperatures. The
contribution is listed as follows.
1) A comprehensive model of the AA-CAES based energy hub with
multi-temperature heat demands is proposed. Electric heater
and heat pump are employed to produce high-temperature
thermal energy and low-temperature thermal energy, respec-
tively. The ﬂow of heat transfer ﬂuid across high-temperature
and low-temperature thermal storage tanks are explicitly
considered, allowing modeling the cascaded utilization of heat.
2) A bi-level optimization model for optimal bidding and sched-
uling of AA-CAES based energy hub in the day-ahead distribu-
tion market is suggested. The upper level is the power purchase
and self-scheduling of the energy hub, aiming at minimizing the
daily operation cost; the lower level represents the alternating-
current optimal power ﬂow based market clearing which de-
termines the electricity transaction price. As the lower-level
market clearing problem is non-linear, existing approaches
encounter difﬁculties to solve such a bilevel problem.
3) A direct search algorithm to solve the bi-level model is devel-
oped. Radial basis function is used to create a surrogate model,
which can be solved with lower computational efforts. The
surrogate model is updated dynamically when more sampling
points in unvisited regions are available. The proposed method
solves the market clearing problem via convex relaxation rather
than replacing it with optimality condition, hence is scalable to
the size of the power grid. The proposed method outperforms
Bayesian Optimization (BO) method, the state-of-the-art sur-
rogate method.
The rest of the paper is organized as follows. The detailed model
of the AA-CAES based energy hub is depicted in section 2. The bi-
level optimization model for bidding and scheduling in the day-
ahead market is presented in Section 3. The radial basis function
based surrogate optimization algorithm is developed in section 4.
Case studies are reported in Section 5. Conclusions are drawn in
section 6.
2. Modeling of AA-CAES EH
The sketch and detailed architecture of the AA-CAES based en-
ergy hub are shown in Figs. 1 and 2. The AA-CAES consists of a two-
stage compressor, a two-stage expander turbine, an air storage
tank, a thermal energy storage system, and external heating source
including an electric heater and a heat pump. The thermal energy
storage system is made up of three storage tanks with rated tem-
perature of 300 /C14 C (high-temperature tank), 120 /C14 C (low-temper-
ature tank) and 25 /C14 C (ordinary-temperature tank). During
charging process, the compressors consumes electricity purchased
from the distribution system, producing high-pressure air which is
stored in a storage tank or salt cavern; the heat generated by the
compression process is collected by the heat exchanger and stored
in the high-temperature heat tank. During discharging process, the
high-pressure air is ﬁrstly reheated and then ﬂows into the
expander. The throttle valves are used to adjust the air pressure in
the last-stage compressor and ﬁrst-stage expander. The thermal
energy produced by air compression is limited; so the electric
heater and the heat pump are employed to directly heat the high-
temperature tank and low-temperature tank, which serve high-
temperature demand and low-temperature demand, respectively.
The following assumptions are made in this paper.
1) In the air storage tank, the mass and pressure follows ideal gas
equation.
2) The heat capacities of air and heat transfer ﬂuid are constant.
3) The temperature in the air storage tank is constant which is
equal to the ambient temperature. The temperatures in the
three heat tanks are constant.
4) Power consumption of ﬂuid booster pump is neglected. Air
pressure loss and heat loss are neglected.

Surrogate optimization method is popular for black-box opti-
mization problem without derivative information, which means it

The convergence performance of the algorithm depends on the
parameters of penalty terms. The parameters g, z and u can be

5.3. Sensitivity analysis
We also explore the impact of AA-CAES EH parameters and local
load scale on the total operating cost, cross-grade supply and
electric energy storage. The effect of heat exchanger ef ﬁciency and
each stage compressor and turbine ef ﬁciency on the total operating
expense is shown in Figs. 17 and 18 , respectively. The studied
benchmark parameters are simultaneously multiplied by the same
ampliﬁcation coef ﬁcient.
From Fig. 17, it can be observed that the operating cost decreases
with the increase of heat exchanger ef ﬁciency and the result is
opposite in Fig. 18. Higher heat exchanger ef ﬁciency means less
thermal loss and can thus reduce power procurement cost. How-
ever, as is shown in Table 6 , higher compressor and turbine ef ﬁ-
ciency results in lower inlet and outlet air temperature gap of heat
exchangers, causing less thermal conversion and storage during
compression stage and less heat absorption in air expansion pro-
cess. Since the ef ﬁciency of the two compressors increases more,
the reduction of compression heat storage is more than the
decrease in expansion heat requirement. Therefore, more elec-
tricity needs procuring and converting to heat generation.
Figs. 19 and 20 present the variation of the total operating cost
with changes in thermal and electric loads. Moreover, cross-grade
supply curves under different levels of thermal load are plotted in
Fig. 21 and air storage SOCs at different electric load levels are
provided in Fig. 22.
From Figs. 19 and 20, the total operating cost increases with the
extending loads. In Fig. 21, high-temperature storage supplies more
heat before 10 a.m. when low-temperature demand gradually be-
comes higher. And Fig. 22 illustrates that the charge and discharge
capacity of AA-CAES is not necessarily related to the electric load
level. Nonetheless, AA-CAES basically tends to store power in early
hours of a day and largely release in later peak hours, realizing
efﬁcient energy utilization.
